title: Cut essentially all traditional ramp, because a turn-two Arcane Signet is slower than a turn-two Merfolk Looter when the deck's clock is dredge velocity rather than mana.
summary: The commander's exile-copy-cast trigger invites a two-card graveyard combo, and the author deliberately builds away from it, running a looter-plus-dredge engine instead that activates at instant speed in response to graveyard hate. The no-ramp decision is argued on mulligan and sequencing grounds rather than curve: ramp muddies which opening hands are keepable. Uldaros bridges to the mass-reanimation top end by casting a cheap reanimate effect that returns a spell-recurring creature, and the manabase runs multi-type lands so card-type-counting payoffs stay live.

notes: A stated and defended deckbuilding heresy — no ramp — with the sequencing reasoning behind it rather than an assertion.
Pre-release commander: the rank and deck count are still forming and should be re-read once the set is out.
